description: Between **1966** and **1976**, **Mao Zedong** launched a purge of extreme violence to take power back. Red Guards, chaos, then the pragmatic turn of **Deng Xiaoping**.

hero.hook: When a head of state calls on the young to destroy his own party.

blocks.text: Between **1966** and **1976** China went through one of the darkest periods in its modern history: the Cultural Revolution. **Mao Zedong**, founder of the People's Republic and head of the Communist Party, was not launching a reform. He was launching a purge to win back absolute power.
By turning the young against the state and against society itself, he caused the persecution of tens of millions of people and the destruction of a huge part of China's heritage.

It all started with the failure of the **[[Great Leap Forward]]** (**1958-1962**): forced collectivization, famine, millions of deaths, Mao's prestige badly shaken. More pragmatic leaders, such as **[[Liu Shaoqi]]** (the country's president) and **[[Deng Xiaoping]]**, took the economy back in hand.

blocks.caption: Mao Zedong, the “Great Helmsman,” at the center of the personality cult

blocks.text: Mao went around the Party. In **1966** his **[[Dazibao]]** (a wall poster) titled “Bombard the headquarters” accused the leadership of being “revisionists.” The head of state was declaring war on his own administration.
At 72, Mao swam in the Yangtze in July **1966**. Propaganda claimed an impossible record of 15 km in 65 minutes: proof that he was “ready for battle.”

sections.title: After the failure of the Great Leap

blocks.text: Millions of high school and university students formed the **[[Red Guards]]**. Their mission: destroy the “four olds” (ideas, culture, customs, habits). Their bible: the Little Red Book, a collection of quotations from Mao.

blocks.caption: Red Guards brandishing the Little Red Book

blocks.text: Teachers humiliated, officials dragged through the streets, schools closed: ideological “purity” came before everything else. Wearing Western clothes or owning a foreign book could cost you dearly.
In Beijing, Red Guards tried to make the red light the signal to “go,” because red was the revolutionary color.

sections.title: The fury of the Red Guards

blocks.text: From **1967** on, rival Red Guard factions were killing each other. Mao sent in the **[[People's Liberation Army]]**, the Chinese army, and shipped **17 million** young city dwellers off to the countryside to be “re-educated.”

At the top, the fight over the succession set the radicals of the **[[Gang of Four]]**, including Mao's wife **[[Jiang Qing]]**, against the survivors of the purges. Mao's death on **September 9, 1976**, and then the arrest of the Gang of Four, closed the decade of chaos.

The human cost is put at between **500,000** and **2 million** direct deaths, without counting the lives wrecked. In **1981** the Party admitted a “grave error” while keeping Mao as father of the nation.
**[[Deng Xiaoping]]**, purged twice, imposed an opening of the economy: “It does not matter whether the cat is white or black, as long as it catches mice.” China moved from class struggle to growth.

events.detail: Factional fighting, and the young sent to the countryside.
events.title: Peak of the violence

blocks.text: The Cultural Revolution (**1966-1976**) was a decade of purges launched by Mao to take power back, driven by the **[[Red Guards]]** and finally closed by the pragmatism of **[[Deng Xiaoping]]**.

sections.title: The reckoning, then the pragmatic turn
